extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: Common Corpus is the largest open dataset for language model pre-training, containing approximately 2 trillion tokens. The data assembled are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses. The dataset contains a wide variety of languages, ranging from the main European languages to low-resource ones, and includes a large portion of code data. It is composed of six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Web, Open Code, and Open Semantic.
extraction.license: Mixed permissive licenses including Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0
extraction.creator: PleIAs
extraction.inLanguage: Multilingual (English, French, German, Spanish, Latin, Italian, Polish, Greek, Portuguese, Russian, and many others including low-resource languages)
extraction.citeAs: Langlais et al., Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training, 2025, arXiv:2506.01732
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Common Corpus was assembled from multiple sources including Collections As Data (CAD) dumps from cultural heritage institutions, APIs (Internet Archive, Delpher, Gallica, Biblioteca, OpenAlex, Wikimedia Enterprise), partnerships (Wikimedia Deutschland for Wikidata), and aggregation of existing open datasets (Europarl, Caselaw Access Project, CourtListener, EUR-lex, USPTO, The Stack v1 and v2, SEC EDGAR, WTO documents, AMF, TED EU Tenders, GATT Library, YouTube Commons, StackExchange). Data was collected either through full dumps or resource-by-resource via APIs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Document analysis, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: public domain cultural heritage content from national libraries (French National Library/Gallica, Library of Congress, Biblioteca Digital Hispánica, Delpher, Europeana, BnL, New Zealand Papers Past), financial and legal documents (SEC EDGAR, WTO, AMF, EU TED Tenders, GATT Library, EUR-lex, USPTO), scientific articles from OpenAlex and arXiv, code from The Stack v1 and v2 (GitHub), Wikipedia/Wikisource via Wikimedia Enterprise, Wikidata, YouTube CC-By videos, and StackExchange (from The Pile).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Ongoing effort since 2023/2024, with current version released February 2025 for the Paris AI Summit. Documents span from the 15th century to 2024.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: OCR correction using OCRonos (Llama 3 8B-based model) for deteriorated text; replacement of PII with fictitious but realistic values using Microsoft's Presidio with custom regex patterns; toxicity filtering via synthetic rewriting or removal using Celadon classifier; Wikidata translation of RDF triples into natural language sequences across 300 languages.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text segmentation using Segmentext tool; OCR error detection using OCRoscope (cld2-based) and OCRerrcr (DeBERTa-v2 400M parameters); OCR correction using OCRonos; license filtering to retain only permissible licenses; for Open Code: removal of files with non-desired extensions (SVG, csv, json, json5, jsonld, python-traceback, unity3d-asset, numpy, http), removal of files with 75%+ digits, replacement of [\r]+\n with \n; PII removal using Presidio; toxicity filtering using Celadon classifier across five dimensions (race/origin bias, gender/sexuality bias, religious bias, ability bias, violence/abuse).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For toxicity classification training data: 2M annotated samples used to train Celadon across five toxicity dimensions. Documents carry metadata including source URL, license, language(s), collection/domain, and creation year.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Segmentext (text segmentation), OCRoscope (OCR quality detection based on cld2), OCRerrcr (DeBERTa-v2-style 400M parameter model for OCR error detection), OCRonos (Llama 3 8B-based OCR correction model), Microsoft Presidio (PII identification), Celadon (DeBERTa-v3-small ~140M parameter multilingual toxicity classifier), fastText (language identification)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus is an evolving resource. HuggingFace ensures archiving of past versions for reproducibility. Continued collection of data in European languages as part of the LLMs4EU project, with planned expansion to African languages (Swahili, Wolof, Bambara). Available as 10,000 parquet files on HuggingFace.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset historically contained Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses. These were identified using Microsoft's Presidio and custom regex patterns and replaced with fictitious but realistic values to comply with GDPR. The dataset contains multilingual data across multiple languages and cultures.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Common Corpus aims to support pre-training of fully open and auditable LLMs while meeting legal and regulatory requirements (including EU AI regulations). It contributes to open science research in LLMs, makes French a high-resource language, and enables reproducible research. It serves as critical infrastructure for open science and the AI Commons.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Historical documents in Open Culture contain outdated cultural norms and biases regarding ethnic groups, women, and violence that do not meet modern ethical standards. Open Science collection has limited linguistic diversity with ~85% of documents in English. The corpus reflects biases inherent to the sources (e.g., Western/European institutional focus). Toxicity filtering via Celadon was applied across five dimensions (race/origin, gender/sexuality, religion, ability, violence/abuse) to mitigate these biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Common Corpus does not cover the entire range of available open resources (open data paradox). Coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow. The 2 trillion tokens is suitable for pre-training models of limited size; larger models require more data. The dataset does not contain instruction-tuning data and is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning. Curation methods cannot achieve 100% accuracy - OCR errors remain. License identification at web scale remains challenging. Open Science is ~85% English. Historical documents may contain deteriorated or machine-generated text.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training of Large Language Models and Small Language Models. Already used by Anthropic, Pleias 1.0 family (350M, 1.2B, 3B parameters), Barcelona Supercomputing Center's Salamandra series (2B, 7B, 40B), Lucie 7B French SLM, NeKo generalist language correction model by Nvidia. Also used for creating multimodal datasets (FineVideo, Mosel), classifiers, synthetic datasets, benchmarks, RAG models (Pleias-RAG-350M, Pleias-RAG-1B), vision-language models for document processing, historical language models, and creative writing models.
